note: Applied Chemistry (calculations verified in Python) and experiment/scenario Biology questions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of moles in 11 g of carbon(IV) oxide is (C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO₂ = 12 + 32 = 44 g/mol; n = 11/44 = 0.25 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of 0.5 mol of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV), CaCO₃, is (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100 g/mol; mass = 0.5 × 100 = 50 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume occupied by 8 g of oxygen gas at s.t.p. is (O = 16, molar volume = 22.4 dm³)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium trioxonitrate(V), NH₄NO₃, is (N = 14, H = 1, O = 16)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound contains 40% calcium, 12% carbon and 48% oxygen by mass. Its empirical formula is (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Mole ratio: Ca 40/40 = 1, C 12/12 = 1, O 48/16 = 3 ⇒ CaCO₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g). The volume of oxygen required to burn 10 dm³ of hydrogen completely is
questions.explanation: Gas volumes are in the ratio of the coefficients: 2 : 1, so 10 dm³ of H₂ needs 5 dm³ of O₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of molecules in 4.4 g of carbon(IV) oxide is (C = 12, O = 16, Avogadro's number = 6.02 × 10²³)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 4 g of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in water to make 500 cm³ of solution. The concentration of the solution is (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: n = 4/40 = 0.1 mol; volume = 0.5 dm³; concentration = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 25.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ NaOH was exactly neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of HCl. The concentration of the acid is
questions.explanation: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O (1 : 1). CₐVₐ = CᵦVᵦ ⇒ Cₐ = (0.10 × 25)/20 = 0.125 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 25 cm³ of 0.20 mol/dm³ NaOH required 12.5 cm³ of H₂SO₄ for complete neutralisation. The concentration of the acid is
questions.explanation: 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. n(NaOH) = 0.005 mol ⇒ n(H₂SO₄) = 0.0025 mol in 0.0125 dm³ ⇒ 0.20 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 6.5 g of zinc reacts completely with excess dilute hydrochloric acid. The volume of hydrogen produced at s.t.p. is (Zn = 65, molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. n(Zn) = 6.5/65 = 0.1 mol ⇒ 0.1 mol H₂ = 0.1 × 22.4 = 2.24 dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 25 g of calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) is heated strongly until no further change, the mass of solid residue is (CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56)
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. 100 g gives 56 g of CaO, so 25 g gives 25 × 56/100 = 14 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas occupies 300 cm³ at 27 °C. Its volume at 127 °C at the same pressure is
questions.explanation: Charles' law with kelvin temperatures: V₂ = 300 × 400/300 = 400 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 200 cm³ of a gas at 760 mmHg is allowed to expand until its pressure falls to 380 mmHg at constant temperature. Its new volume is
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ ⇒ 760 × 200 = 380 × V₂ ⇒ V₂ = 400 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 500 cm³ of a gas was collected at 27 °C and 700 mmHg. Its volume at s.t.p. is approximately

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Under the same conditions, hydrogen (H₂ = 2) diffuses faster than oxygen (O₂ = 32) by a factor of
questions.explanation: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M, so rate(H₂)/rate(O₂) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A vessel contains oxygen at a partial pressure of 300 mmHg and nitrogen at a partial pressure of 450 mmHg. The total pressure in the vessel is
questions.explanation: Dalton's law: total pressure = sum of partial pressures = 300 + 450 = 750 mmHg.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of a 0.01 mol/dm³ solution of hydrochloric acid is
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid, fully ionised: [H⁺] = 10⁻² ⇒ pH = −log(10⁻²) = 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of a 0.001 mol/dm³ solution of sodium hydroxide is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following salts gives an acidic solution when dissolved in water?
questions.explanation: NH₄Cl comes from a strong acid and a weak base; the NH₄⁺ ion hydrolyses to release H⁺. Na₂CO₃ and CH₃COONa are alkaline, NaCl is neutral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A student adds a few drops of methyl orange to a beaker of dilute hydrochloric acid. The solution turns
questions.explanation: Methyl orange is red in acidic solution (pH below 3.1) and yellow in alkaline solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The quantity of electricity required to deposit 0.1 mol of copper from a solution of Cu²⁺ ions is (F = 96,500 C/mol)
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu: 2 mol of electrons per mole of copper ⇒ 0.1 × 2 × 96,500 = 19,300 C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A current of 0.5 A is passed through silver trioxonitrate(V) solution for 965 s. The mass of silver deposited is (Ag = 108, F = 96,500 C/mol)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The time required to deposit 6.5 g of zinc from a solution of Zn²⁺ ions using a current of 2 A is (Zn = 65, F = 96,500 C/mol)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V, the e.m.f. of the cell Zn(s)|Zn²⁺(aq)||Cu²⁺(aq)|Cu(s) is
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode) = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During the electrolysis of dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid with platinum electrodes, the ratio of the volume of hydrogen to oxygen produced is
questions.explanation: Water is decomposed: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂, so hydrogen (cathode) : oxygen (anode) = 2 : 1 by volume.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄ is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation number of chromium in Cr₂O₇²⁻ is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion of methane is −890 kJ/mol. The heat released when 2 mol of methane burn completely is
questions.explanation: Heat released = 2 × 890 = 1,780 kJ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of neutralisation of HCl by NaOH is −57 kJ/mol. The heat evolved when 0.5 mol of HCl is completely neutralised is
questions.explanation: 0.5 mol × 57 kJ/mol = 28.5 kJ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 0.65 g of zinc granules reacted completely with excess acid in 50 s. The average rate of the reaction is
questions.explanation: Rate = mass reacted/time = 0.65/50 = 0.013 g/s.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which change will increase the rate of reaction between marble chips and dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.D: grinding the marble to a powder
questions.explanation: Powdering increases the surface area in contact with the acid, so more collisions occur per second.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The rate of a certain reaction doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature. If the reaction takes 40 minutes at 20 °C, at 40 °C it will take about
questions.explanation: A 20 °C rise = two doublings ⇒ rate × 4 ⇒ time ÷ 4 = 10 minutes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH = −92 kJ. The yield of ammonia is increased by
questions.explanation: Le Chatelier: 4 mol of gas become 2, so high pressure favours NH₃; the forward reaction is exothermic, so low temperature favours it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At equilibrium, a mixture contains 0.2 mol/dm³ H₂, 0.2 mol/dm³ I₂ and 0.8 mol/dm³ HI. For H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), the equilibrium constant Kc is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Adding a catalyst to a reaction that has reached equilibrium will
questions.B: shift the equilibrium to the left
questions.C: not change the position of equilibrium
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up the forward and backward reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but its position and Kc are unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chlorine consists of 75% ³⁵Cl and 25% ³⁷Cl. Its relative atomic mass is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of neutrons in an atom of ²³₁₁Na is
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element X has 17 electrons. Which statement about X is correct?
questions.D: It is in Group 7 and Period 3
questions.explanation: Configuration 2, 8, 7: three shells ⇒ Period 3; seven outer electrons ⇒ Group 7 (a halogen that forms X⁻ ions).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following substances has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride is an ionic solid held by strong electrostatic forces; the others are simple molecular substances with weak intermolecular forces.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. The volume of oxygen at s.t.p. needed to burn 1 mol of ethanol completely is (molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: 3 mol of O₂ are needed: 3 × 22.4 = 67.2 dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A student bubbles two gases, ethane and ethene, separately through bromine water. The bromine water is decolourised by
questions.explanation: Ethene is unsaturated (C=C) and adds bromine, decolourising it; ethane is saturated and does not react.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The product formed when ethanoic acid is warmed with ethanol in the presence of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is
questions.explanation: Acid + alcohol → ester + water (esterification); ethanoic acid and ethanol give ethyl ethanoate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The molecular formula of the alkane with five carbon atoms is
questions.explanation: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; for n = 5, H = 12 ⇒ C₅H₁₂ (pentane).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A sample of water forms a scum with soap. After boiling, the water lathers easily. The hardness was caused by
questions.explanation: Hardness removed by boiling is temporary hardness, caused by Ca(HCO₃)₂ or Mg(HCO₃)₂, which decompose on heating.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which metal will displace copper from copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution?
questions.explanation: Only a metal higher than copper in the activity series can displace it; zinc is more reactive than copper, the others are less reactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The catalyst used in the Contact process for the manufacture of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is
questions.explanation: V₂O₅ catalyses 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ in the Contact process; iron is the Haber-process catalyst.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A food sample turns blue-black with iodine solution but gives no precipitate with Benedict's solution. The sample contains
questions.explanation: Blue-black with iodine indicates starch; a negative Benedict's test means no reducing sugar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s) is an example of a
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal (zinc) takes the place of a less reactive one (copper) in its compound — a displacement (redox) reaction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt), the expected percentage of short plants in the offspring is
questions.explanation: Tt × Tt gives TT : Tt : tt in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1; only tt (one quarter) is short.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A man of blood group AB marries a woman of blood group O. The possible blood groups of their children are
questions.explanation: The father gives either Iᴬ or Iᴮ, the mother always gives i; children are IᴬI (group A) or IᴮI (group B).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Colour blindness is a sex-linked recessive trait. A carrier woman marries a man with normal vision. The probability that a son will be colour-blind is
questions.explanation: Sons get their X chromosome from the mother; she is XᴬXᵃ, so half of her sons receive Xᵃ and are colour-blind.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Red-flowered and white-flowered four o'clock plants produce offspring with pink flowers. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Neither allele masks the other; the heterozygote shows a blended (intermediate) phenotype — incomplete dominance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A tall plant of unknown genotype was crossed with a short plant (tt). The offspring were 50% tall and 50% short. The genotype of the tall parent is
questions.explanation: This is a test cross; a 1 : 1 ratio means the tall parent gave T half the time and t half the time — it is heterozygous, Tt.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A food sample gives a brick-red precipitate when boiled with Benedict's solution. The food contains
questions.explanation: Benedict's solution changes from blue to brick-red when heated with a reducing sugar such as glucose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A food sample rubbed on a piece of paper leaves a translucent spot that does not disappear on drying. The food contains
questions.explanation: The grease-spot test: fats and oils leave a permanent translucent mark on paper.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A potted plant was kept in a dark cupboard for 48 hours and a leaf was then tested for starch. The result was negative because
questions.B: starch cannot be tested in the dark
questions.C: the plant used up its stored starch and could not photosynthesise without light
questions.D: iodine does not work on old leaves
questions.explanation: Without light there is no photosynthesis; the starch already in the leaf is converted to sugar and used, so the leaf becomes destarched.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Part of a destarched leaf was covered with black paper and the plant was placed in sunlight for six hours. When tested with iodine, only the uncovered part turned blue-black. This shows that
questions.C: carbon(IV) oxide is necessary for photosynthesis
questions.explanation: The only difference between the two parts of the leaf was light; starch formed only where light reached.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A destarched variegated leaf (green and white patches) was exposed to light for several hours and then tested with iodine. Only the green parts turned blue-black. This shows that
questions.D: the white parts have no stomata
questions.explanation: Both parts received light, water and CO₂; only the green parts contain chlorophyll and only they made starch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A red blood cell placed in distilled water swells and bursts because
questions.A: water enters the cell by osmosis
questions.B: water leaves the cell by osmosis
questions.C: salt enters the cell by diffusion
questions.explanation: Distilled water is hypotonic to the cell contents, so water moves in by osmosis; with no cell wall the cell bursts (haemolysis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Fresh potato strips placed in a concentrated salt solution for an hour became soft and flabby because
questions.B: the cells gained water and burst
questions.C: water moved out of the cells by osmosis
questions.D: the starch was converted to sugar
questions.explanation: The salt solution is hypertonic to the cell sap, so water leaves the cells and they become flaccid (plasmolysed).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Lime water in a sealed flask containing germinating bean seeds turned milky after a few hours. This shows that germinating seeds
questions.explanation: Lime water turns milky with carbon(IV) oxide, released by the respiring seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During a 100 m sprint an athlete's leg muscles accumulate lactic acid because
questions.B: oxygen supply cannot meet demand, so anaerobic respiration occurs
questions.C: the blood carries too much oxygen
questions.explanation: When oxygen cannot be delivered fast enough, muscle cells break down glucose without oxygen, producing lactic acid (oxygen debt).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: On a very hot day a person produces a small volume of concentrated urine because
questions.A: the kidneys stop working in heat
questions.B: less water is lost through sweat
questions.C: more water is reabsorbed in the kidney tubules under the influence of ADH
questions.explanation: Sweating lowers blood water content; the pituitary releases more ADH, the tubules reabsorb more water and the urine becomes concentrated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When a person touches a hot pot, the hand is withdrawn before any pain is felt. This is because
questions.A: the reflex is coordinated by the spinal cord, not the brain
questions.explanation: A spinal reflex arc (receptor → sensory neurone → spinal cord → motor neurone → muscle) is faster than the message reaching the brain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person whose pancreas produces too little insulin is likely to have
questions.A: low blood glucose and no glucose in the urine
questions.B: high blood glucose and glucose in the urine
questions.explanation: Insulin lowers blood glucose; without enough of it, glucose stays high and spills into the urine (diabetes mellitus).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → lizard → hawk, if a pesticide kills most of the lizards, the immediate effect will be
questions.D: no change in the other populations
questions.explanation: Grasshoppers lose their predator and increase; hawks lose their food and decrease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A 1 m² quadrat was thrown 10 times at random in a 200 m² field. A total of 50 plants of species X were counted. The estimated population of X in the field is
questions.explanation: Mean density = 50/10 = 5 plants per m²; population = 5 × 200 = 1,000.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A single mango tree supports thousands of caterpillars, which are eaten by a few dozen birds. The pyramid of numbers for this food chain is
questions.explanation: One producer supports many consumers, so the base (the tree) is narrower than the next level — the pyramid is inverted.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Water poured onto a soil sample drained through in a few seconds and the soil held very little of it. The soil is most likely
questions.explanation: Sandy soil has large particles and large air spaces, so it drains quickly and retains little water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Untreated sewage was discharged into a river and, a few days later, many fish died. The most likely cause is that
questions.A: the sewage poisoned the fish directly
questions.B: bacteria decomposing the sewage used up the dissolved oxygen
questions.explanation: Decomposers multiply on the organic waste and consume dissolved oxygen, so the fish suffocate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In industrial areas of England, dark-coloured peppered moths became more common than light-coloured ones. The best explanation is that
questions.B: dark moths were better camouflaged on soot-covered trees and less often eaten by birds
questions.explanation: This is natural selection: the better-camouflaged variety survived and reproduced more.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A flower has small dull petals, no scent, no nectar and long feathery stigmas hanging outside the flower. It is most likely pollinated by
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers do not need to attract animals; feathery stigmas catch pollen from the air.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A seedling kept in a box with light entering from one side bent towards the light. This response is called
questions.explanation: Growth of a shoot towards light is positive phototropism, caused by auxin accumulating on the shaded side.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When the biceps contracts the triceps relaxes and the arm bends; when the triceps contracts the biceps relaxes and the arm straightens. The two muscles are described as
questions.explanation: Muscles that produce opposite movements at a joint form an antagonistic pair.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A cell seen under the microscope has a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole. It is most likely a
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts and a cellulose cell wall occur only in plant cells; leaf cells are photosynthetic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An animal has moist skin without scales, lays its eggs in water and its young breathe with gills while the adults breathe with lungs. It is
questions.explanation: Amphibians such as frogs and toads have a water-dwelling larval stage (tadpole) and lung-breathing adults.
